A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Thinking in Space research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VSI-Bench model and human evaluations, error analyses, and experiments with linguistic prompting and cognitive maps.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds cognitive-map evaluations on further models, frame-sampling experiments, a caption-based comparison, and subset results.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, self-explanation analysis, linguistic prompting, and proposed cognitive-map procedures remain unchanged. Additional models reuse existing procedures; the new caption-based pipeline is a comparison method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same eight VSI-Bench tasks and 288 videos from ScanNet, ScanNet++, and ARKitScenes, alongside the existing VideoMME control. The additional subset and input-processing experiments stay within this coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix B.5 extends the cognitive-map comparison beyond Gemini-1.5 Pro to LLaVA-Video-7B and 72B. Appendix C.4 adds Socratic GPT-4o using LLaVA-Video-72B captions. Existing LLaVA-NeXT-Video table rows are relabeled LLaVA-Video while retaining their scores, without establishing a separate model replacement.

E3.justification: Reported InternVL2 frame budgets change from 8 to 32 frames (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 9), materially changing conditions for three benchmark models. v2 also introduces frame-count sensitivity experiments spanning 8–64 frames and an additional 560-question subset selected to match full-set model performance. The original 400-question subset and ACC/MRA metrics remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether cognitive-map locality and prompting benefits generalize across models, whether frame sampling limits performance, and how caption-mediated answering compares with direct video input. The optimized subset adds a representativeness check. The existing blind-evaluation analysis is retained and relocated to Appendix C.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or run-to-run variability. The existing sampling and voting counts for self-consistency and Tree-of-Thoughts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: With revised frame settings, Table 1 replaces InternVL2-2B/8B/40B averages of 27.4/34.6/36.0 with 26.5/37.5/37.0, changing rankings. New Table 6 reports cognitive-map effects of 36.0 to 42.0 for LLaVA-Video-72B and 40.0 to 32.0 for 7B. Table 7 adds Socratic GPT-4o at 29.3 versus standard GPT-4o at 34.0. Figure 11 and Table 11 add frame-sampling and 560-question subset results.

T1.justification: The MRA definition, cognitive-map distance calculations, and correctness criterion are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims: VSI-Bench exposes subhuman spatial intelligence, spatial reasoning is the principal bottleneck, linguistic prompting is ineffective overall, and cognitive maps can improve distance reasoning.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 introduces a model-dependent qualification: cognitive-map prompting hurts the 7B model, tentatively attributed to limited capacity and poorer maps. Appendix C.3 newly argues that frame count is not the primary bottleneck. Section 7 modestly sharpens the emphasis on visual working memory and implicit scene reconstruction.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies the existing repeated-video input as [Video] [Context] [Video], with a system instruction identifying the repetition. v2 also identifies the Socratic captioner and answering model and revises documented frame counts. Project, evaluation-code, and dataset access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds five works, including VideoEspresso and Video Instruction Tuning with Synthetic Data. Section 7 incorporates additional spatial/video reasoning citations and refines the benchmark's positioning, while preserving the existing related-work framework.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. The blind-evaluation discussion moves into Appendix C.4, Appendix B.5 and several explanatory paragraphs are added, and model names and acknowledgments receive limited edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds the frame-sampling plot and four tables for cognitive-map, Socratic, and subset results. The original blind-evaluation figure moves from the main text to Appendix C.4, with subsequent renumbering and reflow. Existing visual examples and the overall presentation style are retained.

improvement.justification: Extending v1's Gemini-only cognitive-map evidence to additional models, including a failure case, and adding frame-sampling and caption controls modestly strengthen the paper's empirical support. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Appendix B.5 claims 8% improvement while Table 6 shows six percentage points, and Appendix C.2 describes new human evaluation although Table 11 contains only model scores. The improvement is therefore limited rather than substantial.
